The text of the Explanation added to Article 15(6) and Article 16(6) by the 103rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 explicitly clarifies that 'economically weaker sections' shall be such as may be notified by the State from time to time, but specifically applies to citizens other than those belonging to the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (OBCs) covered under Articles 15(4), 15(5), and 16(4).

In accordance with Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) Office Memorandum No. 36039/1/2019-Estt (Res) dated 31 January 2019, persons who are not covered under the existing scheme of reservation for SCs, STs, and Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (OBCs) and whose family has gross annual income below Rs. 8.00 lakh are eligible for EWS reservation.

Para 4.1 of the OM specifies that persons whose family has a 'gross annual income below Rs. 8.00 lakh (Rupees eight lakh only)' are to be identified as EWS for the benefit of reservation. 

Key aspects of the income criteria include:

2. The relevant period is the financial year prior to the year of application for the EWS Income and Asset Certificate.
3. 'Family' for this purpose includes the person who seeks the benefit of reservation, his/her parents and siblings below the age of 18 years, as well as his/her spouse and children below the age of 18 years.

questions.question_english: Article 16(4A) of the Constitution empowers the State to provide reservation in matters of promotion in public services. To which specific categories or groups does Article 16(4A) exclusively apply?
options_english: Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs / OBCs)
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes only
Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) of citizens
Persons with Benchmark Disabilities (PwBD)
questions.explanation_english:
Article 16(4A) was introduced into the Constitution by the Constitution (Seventy-Seventh Amendment) Act, 1995, specifically to nullify the effect of the Supreme Court's ruling in Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992), wherein the Court had held that reservation under Article 16(4) is confined only to initial/direct appointments and does not extend to promotions.

Parliament enacted Article 16(4A), which provides: 'Nothing in this article shall prevent the State from making any provision for reservation in matters of promotion, with consequential seniority, to any class or classes of posts in the services under the State in favour of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes which, in the opinion of the State, are not adequately represented in the services under the State.'

Crucially, Article 16(4A) applies EXCLUSIVELY to Scheduled Castes (SC) and Scheduled Tribes (ST). It does not apply to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) or Economically Weaker Sections (EWS). Therefore, reservation in promotion in central/state government employment is constitutionally permissible only for SC and ST categories.
questions.explanation_hindi:
संविधान (77वां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 1995 द्वारा संविधान में अनुच्छेद 16(4A) जोड़ा गया था। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य 'इंद्रा साहनी बनाम भारत संघ (1992)' मामले में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के उस निर्णय के प्रभाव को समाप्त करना था, जिसमें न्यायालय ने कहा था कि अनुच्छेद 16(4) के तहत आरक्षण केवल सीधी/प्रारंभिक नियुक्तियों तक सीमित है और पदोन्नति में लागू नहीं हो सकता।

संसद ने अनुच्छेद 16(4A) जोड़कर यह स्पष्ट प्रावधान किया कि राज्य को 'अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों' के पक्ष में, जिनका राज्य की सेवाओं में पर्याप्त प्रतिनिधित्व नहीं है, पदोन्नति के मामलों में परिणामी वरिष्ठता सहित आरक्षण देने से नहीं रोका जा सकेगा।

महत्वपूर्ण बिंदु यह है कि अनुच्छेद 16(4A) का लाभ विशेष रूप से और केवल 'अनुसूचित जातियों (SC) और अनुसूचित जनजातियों (ST)' पर लागू होता है। यह अन्य पिछड़ा वर्ग (OBC) या आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग (EWS) पर लागू नहीं होता है। अतः सरकारी नौकरियों में पदोन्नति में आरक्षण केवल SC और ST संवर्ग के लिए ही संवैधानिक रूप से मान्य है।

options_english: Part III (Fundamental Rights)
Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy)
Part IVA (Fundamental Duties)
Part IX (The Panchayats and Local Governance)
questions.explanation_english:
Article 46 of the Constitution of India is located within Part IV of the Constitution, which encompasses the Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36 to 51).

Constitutional Framework of Part IV:
1. Non-Justiciability: Under Article 37, the provisions contained in Part IV are not enforceable by any court (non-justiciable through judicial writs). However, Article 37 explicitly affirms that 'the principles therein laid down are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.'
2. Role in Social Welfare: Article 46 serves as a foundational constitutional compass directing executive policy, welfare schemes, educational budgets, and affirmative social action for weaker sections, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes across both central and state education ministries.
questions.explanation_hindi:
भारतीय संविधान का अनुच्छेद 46 संविधान के 'भाग IV' में स्थित है, जिसमें राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व (अनुच्छेद 36 से 51) शामिल हैं।

भाग IV का संवैधानिक ढांचा:
1. गैर-न्यायसंगतता (Non-justiciability): अनुच्छेद 37 के अनुसार, भाग IV के प्रावधान किसी भी न्यायालय द्वारा लागू नहीं कराए जा सकते (अर्थात इनके उल्लंघन पर रिट जारी नहीं की जा सकती)। हालांकि, अनुच्छेद 37 यह स्पष्ट करता है कि ये सिद्धांत 'देश के शासन में मूलभूत हैं और विधि बनाने में इन सिद्धांतों को लागू करना राज्य का कर्तव्य होगा।'
2. सामाजिक कल्याण में भूमिका: अनुच्छेद 46 केंद्र और राज्य सरकारों के लिए एक मार्गदर्शक का कार्य करता है, जो कमजोर वर्गों, अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के कल्याण, छात्रवृत्तियों, छात्रावासों और शैक्षिक बजट के निर्माण में नीतिगत आधार प्रदान करता है।

questions.question_english: Which of the following phrases is explicitly used in Article 15(5) of the Constitution of India regarding the types of educational institutions covered for affirmative action?
options_english: "Only state-owned and state-managed public educational institutions"
"Educational institutions receiving regular financial grant-in-aid from the State"
"Whether aided or unaided by the State, other than minority educational institutions"
"All recognized educational institutions including minority-managed institutions"
questions.explanation_english:
Article 15(5) was inserted into the Constitution of India by the Constitution (Ninety-Third Amendment) Act, 2005 (effective from 20 January 2006) to overcome the effect of judicial pronouncements in the P.A. Inamdar (2005) and T.M.A. Pai Foundation cases regarding reservations in private unaided educational institutions.

The explicit statutory text of Article 15(5) provides that nothing in Article 15 or in sub-clause (g) of clause (1) of Article 19 shall prevent the State from making special provisions by law for the advancement of socially and educationally backward classes of citizens (SEBCs) or SCs/STs relating to their admission to educational institutions, 'including private educational institutions, whether aided or unaided by the State, other than the minority educational institutions referred to in clause (1) of article 30'.

Key takeaways for educational administrators:
1. It covers both government-aided and private unaided non-minority educational institutions (such as private professional colleges, higher education institutions, and schools under the 25% quota under RTE Act Section 12(1)(c)).
2. It expressly excludes minority educational institutions established and administered under Article 30(1) of the Constitution.
questions.explanation_hindi:
संविधान (93वां संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2005 द्वारा भारतीय संविधान में अनुच्छेद 15(5) जोड़ा गया था (जो 20 जनवरी 2006 से प्रभावी हुआ)। इसका उद्देश्य निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त शिक्षण संस्थानों में आरक्षण के संबंध में टी.एम.ए. पाई और पी.ए. इनामदार मामलों में सर्वोच्च न्यायालय के निर्णयों की सीमाओं को दूर करना था।

अनुच्छेद 15(5) के संवैधानिक पाठ में स्पष्ट रूप से उल्लेख किया गया है कि राज्य सामाजिक और शैक्षणिक रूप से पिछड़े वर्गों (SEBCs) या अनुसूचित जातियों/जनजातियों की उन्नति के लिए शिक्षण संस्थानों में प्रवेश के संबंध में विशेष कानून बना सकता है, जिसमें 'निजी शिक्षण संस्थान भी शामिल हैं, चाहे वे राज्य द्वारा सहायता प्राप्त हों या गैर-सहायता प्राप्त हों, किंतु अनुच्छेद 30 के खंड (1) में निर्दिष्ट अल्पसंख्यक शिक्षण संस्थान इसमें शामिल नहीं हैं' (whether aided or unaided by the State, other than the minority educational institutions referred to in clause (1) of article 30)।

शैक्षिक प्रशासकों के लिए प्रमुख बिंदु:
1. यह प्रावधान सरकारी सहायता प्राप्त और निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त दोनों प्रकार के गैर-अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों पर लागू होता है (जैसे आरटीई अधिनियम की धारा 12(1)(c) के तहत 25% आरक्षण)।
2. अनुच्छेद 30(1) के तहत स्थापित एवं प्रशासित भाषाई और धार्मिक अल्पसंख्यक संस्थानों को इस आरक्षण के दायरे से पूरी तरह छूट दी गई है।

questions.question_english: Under Sections 8 and 9 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, which specific statutory duty is imposed on the appropriate Government and local authorities regarding children belonging to disadvantaged groups and weaker sections?
options_english: To provide them with mandatory monthly financial stipends and educational grants
To prevent discrimination and ensure completion of elementary education
To establish dedicated separate neighborhood schools exclusively for their education
To exempt them unconditionally from all minimum age criteria during admission
questions.explanation_english: Sections 8 and 9 of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 delineate the statutory duties of the 'Appropriate Government' and 'Local Authority' respectively. Specifically, Section 8(c) and Section 9(c) state that authorities must 'ensure that the child belonging to weaker section and the child belonging to disadvantaged group are not discriminated against and prevented from pursuing and completing elementary education on any grounds'. This provision prohibits overt and covert discrimination (such as caste-based seating segregation, denying mid-day meals, or exclusion from school activities) and places an affirmative legal obligation on the state administration to track, retain, and support marginalized children throughout the 8-year elementary cycle.
questions.explanation_hindi: निःशुल्क और अनिवार्य बाल शिक्षा का अधिकार (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 8(c) और धारा 9(c) क्रमशः समुचित सरकार (Appropriate Government) और स्थानीय प्राधिकारियों (Local Authorities) पर यह वैधानिक दायित्व सौंपती हैं कि वे 'यह सुनिश्चित करेंगे कि अलाभित समूह (Disadvantaged Group) और दुर्बल वर्ग (Weaker Section) के बालक के साथ कोई भेदभाव न हो और उसे किसी भी आधार पर प्रारंभिक शिक्षा प्राप्त करने तथा उसे पूरा करने से रोका न जाए'। यह प्रावधान विद्यालयों में जाति, वर्ग, लिंग अथवा दिव्यांगता के आधार पर होने वाले किसी भी प्रकार के प्रत्यक्ष या परोक्ष भेदभाव को पूर्णतः प्रतिबंधित करता है और राज्य प्रशासन को प्रत्येक बच्चे की 8 वर्षीय प्रारंभिक शिक्षा का निर्बाध समापन सुनिश्चित करने का आदेश देता है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: How many specified disabilities are recognized under the Schedule of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016?
questions.explanation_english: The Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016 recognizes 21 specified disabilities, substantially expanding the coverage from the 7 conditions recognized under the repealed Persons with Disabilities Act, 1995. The 21 categories include physical disabilities (locomotor disability, leprosy cured, cerebral palsy, dwarfism, muscular dystrophy, acid attack victims, blindness, low-vision, deaf, hard of hearing, speech and language disability), intellectual disabilities (specific learning disabilities, autism spectrum disorder), mental illness, chronic neurological conditions (multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease), blood disorders (haemophilia, thalassemia, sickle cell disease), and multiple disabilities. Under Section 56, the Central Government also possesses the statutory power to notify additional conditions.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की अनुसूची के तहत कुल 21 विनिर्दिष्ट दिव्यांगताओं को मान्यता प्रदान की गई है, जो कि 1995 के पुराने कानून में मान्यता प्राप्त 7 दिव्यांगताओं से तीन गुना अधिक है। इन 21 श्रेणियों में शारीरिक अक्षमताएँ (चलन दिव्यांगता, कुष्ठ रोग मुक्त, सेरेब्रल पाल्सी, बौनापन, मस्कुलर डिस्ट्रॉफी, एसिड अटैक पीड़ित, दृष्टिहीनता, अल्प दृष्टि, बधिर, श्रवण बाधित, वाक् एवं भाषा दिव्यांगता), बौद्धिक अक्षमता (विशिष्ट अधिगम अक्षमता, ऑटिज्म स्पेक्ट्रम), मानसिक रुग्णता, दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी विकार (मल्टीपल स्केलेरोसिस, पार्किंसंस रोग), रक्त विकार (हीमोफिलिया, थैलेसीमिया, सिकल सेल रोग) और बहु-दिव्यांगता शामिल हैं। धारा 56 के तहत केंद्र सरकार नई दिव्यांगताओं को जोड़ने हेतु अधिकृत है।

questions.question_english:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Maintaining a separate section or segregated classroom exclusively for students admitted under the EWS/DG quota in a recognized school violates the principles of inclusive education.
Reason (R): Segregation of schoolchildren on the basis of socio-economic status causes stigmatization, undermines social integration, and violates the non-discrimination mandate of the RTE Act, 2009.
In the context of the two statements, which of the following is correct?
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation_english: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 mandates specified schools and unaided private schools to admit at least 25% of the strength of Class I (or pre-primary) from children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups. The core philosophical foundation of this mandate, as affirmed by the Supreme Court of India in 'Society for Unaided Private Schools of Rajasthan v. Union of India (2012)', is social integration and dismantling socio-economic segregation. Segregating EWS children into separate classrooms, offering them different uniforms, or providing inferior pedagogical attention constitutes unlawful discrimination, creates severe psychological trauma and stigmatization, and directly subverts the RTE mandate. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true, Reason (R) is true, and Reason (R) is the direct and correct explanation of Assertion (A).
questions.explanation_hindi: आरटीई (RTE) अधिनियम, 2009 की धारा 12(1)(c) निजी गैर-सहायता प्राप्त विद्यालयों में प्रारंभिक कक्षा में 25% सीटें आर्थिक रूप से कमजोर वर्ग (EWS) तथा वंचित समूह (DG) के बच्चों के लिए आरक्षित करती है। इस व्यवस्था का मुख्य उद्देश्य सामाजिक समावेशिता (Social Inclusion) को बढ़ावा देना और सामाजिक-आर्थिक दूरियों को पाटना है। जैसा कि सर्वोच्च न्यायालय ने 'सोसाइटी फॉर अनएडेड प्राइवेट स्कूल्स ऑफ राजस्थान बनाम भारत संघ (2012)' मामले में स्पष्ट किया था, EWS बच्चों को सामान्य बच्चों से अलग किसी पृथक सेक्शन में पढ़ाना या उनके साथ अलग व्यवहार करना समानता के सिद्धांत (अनुच्छेद 14) और गैर-भेदभाव के अधिकार (धारा 8/9 RTE) का उल्लंघन है। ऐसा अलगाव बच्चों में हीनभावना और मनोवैज्ञानिक कलंक उत्पन्न करता है। अतः अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सत्य हैं तथा R, A की बिल्कुल सही व्याख्या है। विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।

questions.explanation_english: Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas (KGBVs) were launched in 2004 (and now integrated under Samagra Shiksha) as residential upper primary and secondary schools in Educationally Backward Blocks (EBBs) where female rural literacy is below the national average and the gender gap in literacy is above the national average. Under program guidelines, a minimum of 75% of total admissions are mandatorily reserved for girls belonging to Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), Other Backward Classes (OBC), and Minority communities. The remaining 25% of seats are allocated to girls from families living Below Poverty Line (BPL) irrespective of community, ensuring targeted educational equity for the most marginalized girl children.

The Rehabilitation Council of India, Statutory Body

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 2(b) of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'appropriate Government' is defined in relation to establishments owned, controlled, or substantially financed by the Central Government as the Central Government, and in relation to establishments owned, controlled, or substantially financed by a State Government or Union Territory administration as that respective Government or administration. For schools established, managed, or funded by the Directorate of Education, GNCTD, the appropriate Government is the Government of National Capital Territory of Delhi (GNCTD). The appropriate Government carries statutory responsibilities under the Act for providing barrier-free infrastructure, inclusive education, teacher training, and reasonable accommodations.
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की धारा 2(b) के अनुसार 'समुचित सरकार' का अर्थ केंद्र सरकार के नियंत्रण वाले प्रतिष्ठानों के लिए केंद्र सरकार तथा राज्य सरकार या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश प्रशासन के नियंत्रण वाले प्रतिष्ठानों के लिए संबंधित राज्य सरकार या केंद्र शासित प्रदेश प्रशासन है। शिक्षा निदेशालय, GNCTD द्वारा संचालित अथवा वित्तपोषित विद्यालयों के लिए 'समुचित सरकार' राष्ट्रीय राजधानी क्षेत्र दिल्ली सरकार (GNCTD) है। समुचित सरकार होने के नाते दिल्ली सरकार पर इन विद्यालयों में बाधा-मुक्त वातावरण, समावेशी शिक्षा, विशेष शिक्षक प्रशिक्षण तथा उचित समायोजन सुनिश्चित करने का वैधानिक दायित्व है।

questions.question_english: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Teachers' Cadre) Act, 2019 was enacted to restore the 200-point roster system. What was the critical shift in the definition of the "unit" for preparing the roster under this Act?
options_english: Each academic department or subject
The University/College as a whole
The entire State administrative territory
Each specific faculty or division
questions.explanation_english: The Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Teachers' Cadre) Act, 2019 was passed by Parliament to nullify the impact of the Allahabad High Court judgment (Vivekanand Tiwari case, upheld by the Supreme Court), which had mandated that teacher recruitment reservation rosters be prepared department-wise/subject-wise. Treating individual departments as units severely curtailed SC, ST, and OBC reservation because many departments had only 1 or 2 sanctioned posts, rendering reservation legally inapplicable under the rule that a single isolated post cannot be reserved. Section 3 of the 2019 Act restored social justice by stipulating that for the purpose of reservation in direct recruitment of teachers, the entire 'Central Educational Institution' (the University, College, or deemed-to-be-university as a whole) shall be treated as a single comprehensive unit. This restored the 200-point roster across all departments clubbed by cadre (Professor, Associate Professor, and Assistant Professor), ensuring statutory representation.
questions.explanation_hindi: 'केंद्रीय शैक्षणिक संस्थान (शिक्षक संवर्ग में आरक्षण) अधिनियम, 2019' संसद द्वारा उस न्यायिक संकट को हल करने के लिए लागू किया गया था, जो इलाहाबाद उच्च न्यायालय के उस निर्णय (विवेकानंद तिवारी वाद) के बाद उत्पन्न हुआ था जिसमें रोस्टर को विभाग/विषय-वार लागू करने का निर्देश दिया गया था। विभाग-वार गणना से अधिकांश छोटे विभागों (जहाँ 1 या 2 पद होते हैं) में आरक्षण समाप्तप्राय हो गया था, क्योंकि एकल पद को आरक्षित नहीं किया जा सकता। 2019 के इस ऐतिहासिक अधिनियम की धारा 3 ने यह विधिक व्यवस्था दी कि शिक्षकों के संवर्ग में सीधी भर्ती हेतु आरक्षण रोस्टर तैयार करने के लिए संपूर्ण 'विश्वविद्यालय/महाविद्यालय को एक समग्र इकाई' (University/College as a whole) माना जाएगा। इससे 200-बिंदु रोस्टर प्रणाली पुनः बहाल हुई और विभिन्न विभागों के समान संवर्गों के पदों को एक साथ जोड़कर SC, ST, OBC और EWS के लिए पूर्ण आरक्षण सुनिश्चित किया गया।

questions.question_english: Which of the following conditions is classified under "Chronic Neurological Conditions" in the RPwD Act, 2016?
options_english: Hemophilia
Leprosy cured person
Autism spectrum disorder
Parkinson's disease
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 1(D) of the Schedule to the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, 'Chronic Neurological Conditions' includes two specified medical conditions: (i) Multiple Sclerosis, and (ii) Parkinson's disease. Parkinson's disease is defined as a progressive disease of the nervous system marked by tremor, muscular rigidity, and slow, imprecise movement, chiefly affecting middle-aged and elderly people, associated with degeneration of the basal ganglia of the brain and a deficiency of the neurotransmitter dopamine. Among the other choices, Hemophilia is a Blood Disorder (Section 4), Leprosy Cured Person is classified under Locomotor Disability (Section 1(A)(b)), and Autism Spectrum Disorder is classified under Intellectual Disability / Neurodevelopmental conditions (Section 2).
questions.explanation_hindi: दिव्यांगजन अधिकार अधिनियम, 2016 की अनुसूची के भाग 1(D) के अनुसार 'दीर्घकालिक तंत्रिका संबंधी स्थिति' (Chronic Neurological Conditions) के अंतर्गत दो प्रमुख रोगों को विनिर्दिष्ट किया गया है: (i) मल्टीपल स्केलेरोसिस, और (ii) पार्किंसंस रोग। पार्किंसंस रोग केंद्रीय तंत्रिका तंत्र का एक प्रगतिशील विकार है जो शरीर के कंपन, कठोरता और शारीरिक संतुलन व गति में असमर्थता पैदा करता है। अन्य विकल्पों में, हीमोफिलिया 'रक्त विकार' है, कुष्ठ रोग मुक्त व्यक्ति 'चलन दिव्यांगता' का अंग है, और ऑटिज्म स्पेक्ट्रम विकार 'बौद्धिक दिव्यांगता' के अंतर्गत वर्गीकृत है।

Scheduled Tribes students exclusively

questions.explanation_english: PM YASASVI (Prime Minister Young Achievers Scholarship Award Scheme for Vibrant India for OBCs, EBCs, and DNTs) is a comprehensive umbrella scheme formulated by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment (MoSJE), Government of India. The scheme is specifically tailored to provide financial and educational empowerment to students belonging to Other Backward Classes (OBC), Economically Backward Classes (EBC), and De-Notified, Nomadic and Semi-Nomadic Tribes (DNT) whose annual family parental income does not exceed ₹2.5 lakh. The PM YASASVI umbrella encompasses Pre-Matric Scholarships (Classes IX–X), Post-Matric Scholarships (Class XI to Higher Education), Top Class School Education (in identified top schools across the country), and Top Class College Education.

questions.question_english: If a woman candidate belonging to the Scheduled Caste (SC) category is selected under the horizontal reservation quota for women, how is her appointment accounted for in the reservation roster?
options_english: She is placed in a separate women's roster independently of the SC roster
She is adjusted against the vertical SC category quota
She is counted directly against the open unreserved quota
She consumes two distinct roster points simultaneously
questions.explanation_english: In Rajesh Kumar Daria v. Rajasthan Public Service Commission (2007) 8 SCC 785, the Supreme Court elucidated the precise mechanics of horizontal reservation. Horizontal reservation operates as an interlocking reservation within vertical quotas. When a reserved candidate (such as an SC woman) qualifies under the female horizontal quota, she is adjusted against the vertical quota belonging to her own social category (the SC category quota). This means her selection fills both one vertical post reserved for SCs and simultaneously satisfies the quota requirement for women within the SC group. She does not migrate to an unreserved vacancy, nor does she occupy a separate parallel roster.

questions.question_english: To ensure access to transport under Section 41 of the RPwD Act, 2016, schools utilizing private or government buses must ensure which of the following?

Mandatory retrofitting of all fleet buses with automated wheelchair lifts regardless of financial cost

questions.explanation_english: Section 41 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 mandates that appropriate governments and local authorities take suitable measures to provide accessible transport, including bus stops, transit facilities, and vehicles. questions.question_english:
Consider the following Constitutional Amendments:
I. 77th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1995
II. 81st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000
III. 85th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001

Which of the following aspects of affirmative action in public employment under Article 16 are addressed by these amendments collectively?
options_english: Economic reservation, upper-caste quotas, and private school admission mandates
Promotion reservation, the carry-forward rule for backlog vacancies, and consequential seniority
Mandating 27% reservation for OBC candidates across all central services and PSUs
Abolishing the creamy layer exclusion principle for backward classes in public employment
questions.explanation_english:
The 77th, 81st, and 85th Constitutional Amendments collectively fortified and restructured affirmative action in public employment under Article 16 of the Constitution of India:

1. 77th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1995: Inserted clause (4A) into Article 16 to enable the State to provide reservation in matters of promotion for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, overriding the prohibition on promotional reservation laid down in Indra Sawhney (1992).

2. 81st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000: Inserted clause (4B) into Article 16 to protect the 'carry forward' rule. It provided that unfilled backlog vacancies of a year reserved under clause (4) or (4A) constitute a distinct class that is not subject to the 50% reservation ceiling in succeeding years.

3. 85th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2001: Amended Article 16(4A) with retrospective effect from 17 June 1995 to incorporate the words 'with consequential seniority' for SC and ST employees promoted through reservation rosters, effectively overcoming the judicial 'catch-up rule'.

Together, these three amendments specifically cover: Promotion reservation, the carry-forward rule for backlog vacancies, and consequential seniority.
questions.explanation_hindi:
77वें, 81वें और 85वें संविधान संशोधनों ने सामूहिक रूप से भारतीय संविधान के अनुच्छेद 16 के तहत सार्वजनिक रोजगार में सकारात्मक कार्रवाई के तंत्र को पुनर्गठित और सुदृढ़ किया:

1. 77वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 1995: इसने अनुच्छेद 16 में खंड (4A) जोड़ा, जिससे राज्य को इंद्रा साहनी (1992) के निर्णय के प्रभाव को समाप्त करते हुए अनुसूचित जातियों और अनुसूचित जनजातियों के लिए पदोन्नति में आरक्षण प्रदान करने की शक्ति मिली।

2. 81वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2000: इसने अनुच्छेद 16 में खंड (4B) जोड़ा, जिससे 'कैरी-फॉरवर्ड' (आगे ले जाने का) नियम सुरक्षित हुआ। इसके अनुसार बैकलॉग रिक्तियों को एक अलग वर्ग माना जाता है और उन पर अगले वर्षों में 50% की आरक्षण सीमा लागू नहीं होती।

3. 85वां संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम, 2001: इसने 17 जून 1995 से भूतलक्षी प्रभाव से अनुच्छेद 16(4A) में संशोधन कर 'परिणामी वरिष्ठता सहित' (with consequential seniority) शब्दावली जोड़ी, जिससे सर्वोच्च न्यायालय द्वारा प्रतिपादित 'कैच-अप नियम' का प्रभाव समाप्त हो गया।

अतः ये तीनों संशोधन सामूहिक रूप से: पदोन्नति में आरक्षण, बैकलॉग रिक्तियों के लिए कैरी-फॉरवर्ड नियम और परिणामी वरिष्ठता को संबोधित करते हैं।

questions.question_english: In special education pedagogy, what is the precise distinction between an "Accommodation" and a "Modification" provided to a student with a learning or physical disability?
options_english: Accommodation alters how a student learns and accesses information; modification alters what the student is taught and expected to master
Accommodation applies exclusively to motor/physical disabilities, whereas modification is restricted to intellectual deficits
Accommodation is managed entirely by parents at home, while modification is executed strictly by school subject teachers
There is no substantive pedagogical difference as both terms are legally synonymous and interchangeable
questions.explanation_english:
In special education and inclusive pedagogical terminology, 'Accommodation' and 'Modification' represent two distinct instructional adjustments:
1. Accommodation (समायोजन) changes HOW a student learns and demonstrates knowledge. It removes barriers to learning without lowering or altering instructional standards, curriculum content, or grade-level expectations. Examples include providing extra time during examinations, large-print question papers, audiobooks, preferred seating, or scribes.
2. Modification (संशोधन) changes WHAT a student is taught or expected to learn. It fundamentally alters curriculum expectations, difficulty level, or assessment benchmarks to align with the student's cognitive capabilities. Examples include reducing the complexity of learning objectives, assigning alternate simplified reading materials, or testing on fewer conceptual standards than peers.
questions.explanation_hindi:
समावेशी एवं विशेष शिक्षाशास्त्र में 'समायोजन' (Accommodation) और 'संशोधन' (Modification) दो महत्वपूर्ण और विशिष्ट अवधारणाएं हैं:
1. समायोजन (Accommodation): यह इस बात को परिवर्तित करता है कि छात्र 'कैसे' सीखता है या सूचनाओं तक कैसे पहुंचता है (How one learns)। यह पाठ्यचर्या की कठिनाई, अधिगम मानकों या शैक्षणिक अपेक्षाओं को कम नहीं करता। उदाहरण: परीक्षा में अतिरिक्त समय (Compensatory time) देना, बड़े अक्षरों (Large print) वाली पुस्तकें, ऑडियो पुस्तकें या बैठने की विशेष व्यवस्था।
2. संशोधन (Modification): यह इस बात को परिवर्तित करता है कि छात्र से 'क्या' सीखने की अपेक्षा की जाती है (What is learned)। यह पाठ्यचर्या के मूल स्तर, सामग्री के विस्तार अथवा मूल्यांकन मानकों में बुनियादी बदलाव या सरलीकरण करता है ताकि वह बच्चे की संज्ञानात्मक क्षमताओं के अनुकूल हो सके। उदाहरण: कम कठिन या संक्षिप्त पाठ्यक्रम निर्धारित करना।

questions.explanation_english: The Babu Jagjivan Ram Chhatrawas Yojana (BJRCY) is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme administered by the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India. The core objective of the scheme is to attract Scheduled Caste (SC) students to middle schools, higher secondary schools, colleges, and universities, and prevent dropouts caused by geographic distance and lack of accommodation. The scheme provides central grant-in-aid to State Governments, UT Administrations, Central/State Universities, and non-governmental organizations for the construction of new hostel buildings and the expansion of existing hostels dedicated to SC boys and girls, especially in educationally backward areas.
questions.explanation_hindi: बाबू जगजीवन राम छात्रावास योजना (BJRCY) भारत सरकार के सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय द्वारा संचालित एक महत्वपूर्ण केंद्र प्रायोजित योजना है। इस योजना का मुख्य उद्देश्य अनुसूचित जाति (SC) के बालक-बालिकाओं के लिए मध्य विद्यालयों, उच्च माध्यमिक विद्यालयों, महाविद्यालयों एवं विश्वविद्यालयों में सुरक्षित और समर्पित छात्रावास भवनों का निर्माण तथा मौजूदा छात्रावासों का विस्तार करना है। दूरदराज के ग्रामीण क्षेत्रों से आने वाले एससी छात्रों के लिए आवास की अनुपलब्धता विद्यालय छोड़ने (ड्रॉपआउट) का एक प्रमुख कारण होती है। यह योजना राज्य सरकारों, केंद्रीय/राज्य विश्वविद्यालयों और पात्र संस्थाओं को शत-प्रतिशत अथवा निर्धारित अनुपात में वित्तीय अनुदान देकर छात्रावास सुविधाएं सृजित करती है ताकि दूरी की बाधा को समाप्त किया जा सके।
